title: Directions and Distance Reasoning — Part 3 of 10

questions.question: What does 'cancellation' mean when tracing a multi-step movement path?
options: Stopping the problem early
Movements in opposite directions partially or fully cancel out, reducing the net displacement in that direction
Ignoring every second movement
Converting distance into direction
questions.rationale: When a path includes movement in one direction followed later by movement in the opposite direction, those movements partially or fully cancel out in the net displacement calculation.

questions.question: In a 'long route example' with many turns, why is tracking net displacement more useful than tracking every individual step?
options: Individual steps are always more useful
Because only the net displacement determines the final position and straight-line distance from the start
Because individual steps cannot be tracked at all
Because net displacement ignores all turns
questions.rationale: For finding the final position and straight-line distance from the start, only the net displacement matters — the specific sequence of intermediate steps doesn't change that final result.

questions.question: What is a 'relative turn'?
options: A turn measured in kilometers
A change in direction described relative to the current heading (e.g., 'turn right'), rather than as a fixed compass direction
A turn that only applies to circular routes
A synonym for absolute direction
questions.rationale: A relative turn is described in relation to your current heading, like 'turn right,' as opposed to being stated as a fixed compass direction like 'now face East.'

questions.question: What does a 'turn algorithm' need to track to correctly update heading after a sequence of turns?
options: Only the very first heading
The current heading and the cumulative effect of each turn (degrees and direction) applied to it
Only the total distance traveled
Nothing — turns don't affect heading
questions.rationale: A turn algorithm must maintain the current heading and correctly apply each subsequent turn's degree and direction to it in sequence.

questions.question: If you are heading East and turn 90 degrees left, what is your new heading?
options: South
West
North
East
questions.rationale: Turning 90 degrees left (counter-clockwise) from East lands on North.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'movement direction' and 'heading'?
options: They are always identical
Movement direction is the direction of actual travel; heading is the direction currently faced, which can differ if moving sideways or backward
Heading only applies to circular paths
Movement direction is a synonym for distance
questions.rationale: Movement direction describes which way you're actually traveling, while heading describes which way you're facing — these can differ, for example when moving backward.

questions.question: What does 'forward movement' assume about the relationship between heading and direction of travel?
options: That they are always opposite
That movement direction matches the current heading (moving in the direction you're facing)
That heading is irrelevant to movement
That movement only happens along the x-axis
questions.rationale: Forward movement assumes travel happens in the same direction the entity is currently facing (its heading), which is the simplest and most common case.

questions.question: What do 'spatial relationships' describe between two or more entities?
options: Their names only
How their positions relate to each other, such as one being north of, closer to, or between others
Only their distance from the origin
Whether they are the same color
questions.rationale: Spatial relationships describe how entities' positions relate to one another — north/south of, closer/farther, between, and similar relative descriptions.

questions.question: Why might movement direction and heading NOT match in some problems?
options: This can never happen
If an entity moves sideways or backward relative to the direction it is facing
Only in 3D problems
Because heading is always fixed at North
questions.rationale: An entity can move sideways or backward relative to its facing direction, which is exactly the case where movement direction and heading diverge.

questions.question: What is the benefit of an explicit turn algorithm over informally tracking turns in your head?
options: There is no benefit
It consistently applies the same rule at each step, reducing the chance of a cumulative directional error over a long sequence of turns
It removes the need to know the starting direction
It only works for a single turn
questions.rationale: A consistent, explicit rule applied at each step reduces the risk of a small directional error compounding over a long sequence of turns, which is easy to happen when tracking mentally.
